title: Run and Debug Nodics
readerIntent: Start the intended local topology, understand what loaded, and diagnose startup or runtime failures safely.
priorKnowledge: Complete local setup and understand modules and environments.
owner: nConfig startup and lifecycle contracts plus the selected project environment, server, and node modules
summary: Use MonoServer for fast local integration and modular servers for boundary validation; select topology through metadata-driven environment, server, and node inputs rather than long encoded names.

sections.heading: Choose a topology
items: MonoServer loads the configured local module composition into one process for fast development, debugging, core import, and early end-to-end tests.
Modular servers run selected module compositions as separate processes so HTTP, authentication, registration, provider, timeout, outage, restart, and lifecycle boundaries can be tested.
Server names may repeat across environments because identity is derived from validated ancestry; supply ENV explicitly for deterministic scripts and automation.
A node is an optional instance-specific child of a server. Starting a node requires its server; environment may be inferred only when that server is unique.

sections.heading: Start explicitly
paragraphs: For deterministic local execution use the selected metadata names, for example `ENV=startioLocal SERVER=monoServer npm run start`. For a node use `ENV=startioLocal SERVER=cronServer NODE=cronNode0 npm run start`.
items: If an interactive terminal supplies an ambiguous server without ENV, Nodics offers the discovered environments for selection.
Non-interactive CI, containers, and services fail with candidate environments and an explicit command example instead of waiting for a prompt.
activeModules decides what loads locally; servers.* provides endpoint coordinates and never activates a remote module in the current process.

sections.heading: Local BackOffice topology
items: Begin Axis integration against MonoServer while capabilities are changing rapidly.
Before considering the backend boundaries complete, run at least Profile, CMS staged, CMS online, CronJob, NEMS, DEAP, and BackOffice in their relevant modular processes.
CMS staged and online use distinct systems or schemas; staged authoring/versioning and approved publication must not collapse into one data authority.
A module registers with BackOffice asynchronously; registration failure must not add synchronous latency to unrelated request traffic.

sections.heading: Troubleshoot
items: Confirm the selected environment/server/node, active module list, deterministic index order, parent metadata, effective properties, and servers.* coordinates.
Check mandatory dependency readiness, provider activation, database/search/cache connectivity, bootstrap identity, ports, route exposure, and safe status codes.
Use correlation identifiers and redacted logs; never print passwords, API keys, bearer/refresh tokens, cookies, private keys, or connection credentials.
Stop processes through the lifecycle coordinator so draining and provider cleanup run; hard termination cannot guarantee hooks.
Record exact topology, command, effective non-secret configuration, failure, and focused test evidence when reporting a defect.

sections.heading: Complete guide: How To Run And Debug Nodics
paragraphs: This guide explains the common ways to start Nodics and debug startup or runtime behavior.

sections.heading: Beginner Summary
paragraphs: Running Nodics means starting a selected project, environment, server, and optional node. Debugging means slowing that startup or request execution enough to see which configuration, module, route, service, provider, tenant, or generated artifact is being used.
Before debugging, write down:
Most runtime confusion comes from starting a different server or module set than the one you expected.
items: API path or job/import/event being tested.

sections.heading: Start Normally
paragraphs: Run:

```bash
npm run start
```
Use normal startup when you want to run the application without attaching a debugger.

sections.heading: Start And Pause For Debugging
paragraphs: Run:

```bash
npm run start:debug
```
This starts Node with the inspector and pauses before startup code executes.
Use this when:
Visual Studio Code can attach to port `9229` by default.
items: You need to debug startup configuration.
You need a breakpoint before modules load.
You want to inspect how configuration, schemas, routes, or services are registered.

sections.heading: Start And Attach Later
paragraphs: Run:

```bash
npm run start:inspect
```
This starts the application immediately and exposes the inspector.
Use this when:
items: You want the server running before attaching.
You are debugging an API call, scheduled job, event, or import process.

sections.heading: Using A Different Debug Port
paragraphs: Use a different port when running multiple processes:

```bash
npm run start:debug -- --port=9230
```
Each Node process must use its own inspector port.

sections.heading: Where To Put Breakpoints
paragraphs:
| Problem | Good breakpoint area |
| --- | --- |
| Wrong configuration value | Configuration loading and `CONFIG.get` caller |
| Module not active | Module initializer and selected server `activeModules` |
| Route not found | Router loading, router registration, generated route output |
| Unauthorized API | Header normalization, token validation, route authorization |
| Wrong tenant data | Tenant resolution, DAO/provider resolution, cache/search key creation |
| Controller receives wrong body | Controller request mapping |
| Business rule wrong | Owning service function |
| Generated API wrong | Source schema/router plus generator output |
| Import fails | Import initializer, file/header processing, target dispatch |
| Job does not run | CronJob container, node responsibility, job handler |
| Cache result wrong | Cache key creation, cache policy, invalidation service |

sections.heading: Stop The Application
paragraphs: Use `Ctrl+C` in the terminal.
If a process does not stop, check for remaining Node processes and occupied ports before starting again.

sections.heading: Beginner Troubleshooting
paragraphs:
| Symptom | What to check first |
| --- | --- |
| Breakpoint never hits | Confirm the file is loader-visible and the selected module is active. |
| API returns 404 | Confirm context root, module name, API version, and route registration. |
| API returns 401 or 403 | Confirm token, tenant, route permission, and user group. |
| Data looks stale | Confirm cache and generated artifacts were refreshed. |
| Local server behaves differently than test | Confirm selected environment/server/node and runtime configuration. |
| Debugger cannot attach | Confirm inspector port is unique and the process is running with debug/inspect. |
